interface.title: Scholar Fetcher
interface.field: Literature research / evidence synthesis (systematic and scoping reviews, bibliometrics)
interface.stage_of_work: Finding the literature: the identification stage of a review, from query to an exported corpus
interface.what_it_is_for: Run a scholarly literature search against one or more bibliographic sources, check that every page came back, inspect a deduplicated, sortable results table, and export the corpus as Excel, CSV, BibTeX or RIS without re-running the query. The search record and methods paragraph are produced only by the command line and library in this version, not by this GUI.

data.note: No bundled or uploaded data. All records came live from OpenAlex for the query "large language models evaluation": run 1 used title-abstract, 50 results, deduplication on; run 2 used fulltext, 120 results, deduplication off. OpenAlex was the only source offered. Google Scholar is switched off server-side (SCHOLAR_ENABLED not set), and a banner explains why. The optional contact-email field was empty for every search; an address typed into it during exploration was cleared before any search ran, so none was sent to OpenAlex. The replay (check) used a different query, "large language model benchmark", so its numbers (3 duplicates removed, 47 of 50 shown, 87 'bench' matches, top citation 104, file hash 8423345c) do not match the values in this tree. The replay confirms the behaviour, not the specific values.

features.name: Paged multi-source search with a completeness report
features.general: Run a query against one or more external databases page by page, with a source picker that says what each database reports, then show for each database how many records were asked for and returned, which pages failed, and whether the set is complete, so a partial result is never mistaken for a full one
features.specific: Sources multiselect (help tooltip per source, e.g. OpenAlex 'free and CC0, reports DOI, venue, year, and open-access status, same query returns the same set'; only openalex offered here) plus query, Results, Delay, Match terms in → Search with a progress bar → green 'Identified N · removed K duplicate(s) · showing N of M requested' banner → Per-source detail expander (source, requested, returned, pages_failed, failed_offsets, complete). Multi-source search and the incomplete-page warning were not observed
steps: Pick sources (hover the help icon to see what each reports) and type the query
Set how many results to fetch and the delay between pages
Press Search and watch the progress bar
Read the summary banner and expand Per-source detail to check pages_failed and complete
serves_tasks: Run the search and watch its progress
Confirm no page of results failed to fetch, and treat the set as partial if one did
Choose which databases to search, using what each one reports

features.name: Deduplication, citation-count ranking and provenance columns
features.general: Merge records that describe the same work using a key cascade (id, then DOI, then title and first author), report how many were removed, rank the result by citation count with unknown counts placed last, and record for each field whether it was reported, missing or merged from another source
features.specific: 'Remove duplicate works' checkbox → banner shows 'removed K duplicate(s)' or 'duplicates not removed' → table columns DOI_source (reported/missing), Citations_source (observed), Source, Record_id, Merged_fields. Default order is most-cited first, missing counts last, cut to size after dedup (from the code, not seen on a screen). Unobserved here: cross-source merging, a filled Merged_fields column, and combined Source values such as 'openalex+scholar', since only one source was available
steps: Tick or untick Remove duplicate works
Read the duplicate count in the banner
Scroll the table to the *_source and Merged_fields columns to see where each value came from
serves_tasks: Decide whether duplicate records are merged
See how many duplicates were removed
Check which records lack key metadata and where each value came from

features.name: Sortable results grid (framework-provided)
features.general: Browse a result list in a grid where clicking a header sorts it, a find box highlights matching cells, a column picker hides fields, and a fullscreen mode gives room to read
features.specific: Streamlit's built-in st.dataframe toolbar, not built by this app: click Year/Citations headers to sort; toolbar Search highlights cells matching 'bench' (24 results); Show/hide columns checklist; Fullscreen. Grid state resets on the page rerun after an export
steps: Click a column header once for ascending, again for descending
Open the find box and type a term to highlight matches
Open Show/hide columns and untick fields not needed for screening
Expand to fullscreen and Escape back
serves_tasks: Order the records by a field
Find records containing a term and trim the visible columns
Check which records lack key metadata and where each value came from

features.name: One-search multi-format corpus export
features.general: From a single completed search, download the same record set in several formats (spreadsheet, plain table, two citation-manager formats) without querying the databases again
features.specific: Export row under the table: Excel (.xlsx), CSV (.csv), BibTeX (.bib), RIS (.ris). File names carry a hash of the query only, so the same query with different settings gives the same name
steps: Press BibTeX or RIS to get reference-manager files
Press CSV or Excel to get a screening spreadsheet
Run a changed search and export again for a new corpus
serves_tasks: Export citations for a reference manager
Export a spreadsheet for manual screening or sharing
